# 1e Redeploy, upgrade, rollout, rotation: contract

**Read first:** [server redeploy](../processes/servers/server-redeploy.md), [credential rotation](../processes/servers/credential-rotation.md) (the single-server part; cut-off is Phase 2), [servers module → Server page actions](../modules/servers.md#server-page), designs `RP-Server-redeploy`, `RP-Server-rollout`, `RP-Server-stack`, the 1d contract and every **As built** so far.

**Done when:** an active server can be redeployed, upgraded (or downgraded) and have its parameters edited through a plan screen with per-file diffs, new generated values, endpoint changes and warnings; **Force redeploy** works when nothing differs; a failed deployment offers **Roll back**; a rolling upgrade runs one server at a time and stops at the first failure; **Restart stack**, **Update images**, **Reboot** and **Container logs** work; **Rotate credentials** replaces the rotatable values, verifies them, and restores the old state on failure; the Stack tab shows the last deployment's files (masked) and the deployment history with diffs; every checklist line has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | `deploy.Plan(ctx, serverID, Target{Version, Params, Force})` renders the target for the server (existing generated values + ones the target adds, generated **in memory** for the plan, shown as "new") and compares with the server's **current files** (README rule: the latest succeeded deployment with `uploaded = 1`; a later restart, images or reboot deployment doesn't count): added / changed / removed per path with a masked unified diff, mode changes, new generated values (keys only), endpoints added / removed / changed (a changed URI is flagged "links will get new URIs on their next refresh"; a removed key is a warning), parameters added / removed by the version, the steps that will run. | redeploy.md step 2. |
| Masking | Before diffing, every generated value and secret parameter value (old and new) in file contents is replaced by `•••<key>•••`. Diffs never show secrets. The Stack tab's **Reveal** (per file, admin) shows the real content. Masking needs the values, so a retired server (values erased) shows no file content and no diffs at all (1g). | |
| Nothing to change | No file, endpoint or version difference → "Nothing to change" with **Force redeploy** (strength 1). Nothing is queued without Force. | Edge case. |
| Upgrade parameters | The upgrade form lists the target version's parameters: values carried over by key, new ones prefilled with their default; a new **required** parameter without a default must be filled before the plan is shown; removed ones are listed "will no longer be used" (kept in storage). | redeploy.md. |
| Job type | `servers.deploy`: queue `provisioning`, `MaxAttempts 1`, resource key `server:<id>`. Payload `{server_id, kind (redeploy/upgrade/params), to_version, params, force, rollout_id}`; secret parameters as job secrets `param:<key>`. Steps `connect`, `plan`, `generated-values`, `upload-files`, `redeploy`, `endpoints`, `self-check`, `proxy-test`, `record`. The `redeploy` step runs the version's `steps.redeploy` after its leading `upload-files` (1a's step-order rule). | redeploy.md step 5. |
| Every job type here | `servers.deploy`, `servers.restart`, `servers.update_images`, `servers.reboot`, `servers.rotate`, `servers.restore`, `servers.container_logs`: queue `provisioning`, `MaxAttempts 1`, resource key `server:<id>`, not `Quiet`. | One mutating job per server; the admin retries. |
| Cancel | Every type that writes a deployment has `OnCancelled`: deployment → `failed` (error `cancelled`), `server.redeploy_failed{kind, step, error: "cancelled", cancelled: true}` (`NotifyIf` skips cancelled; the rollout subscriber still sees it). Rotation's `OnCancelled` additionally, when the `generate` step finished, enqueues `servers.restore` in the same transaction (a remote restore can't run inside it), and the log says "restore queued as job #N". | A cancelled job must not leave a deployment `running` or a rollout waiting forever. |
| Recompute | The `plan` step recomputes the plan; if it differs from what the admin saw (a hash of the shown plan in the payload), it logs "the plan was recomputed: …" and continues with the new difference. | redeploy.md rules. |
| Success | `record`: deployment `succeeded` with `files_changed`; server `template_version` and params updated; `server.redeployed{kind, from_version, to_version, files_changed, rollout}`. | |
| Failure | `OnFailed`: deployment `failed`, server stays **active** with its old version and params, `server.redeploy_failed{kind, step, error}`. Endpoints already stored by the `endpoints` step stay (they match what is on the server). | redeploy.md step 6. |
| Roll back | On the latest **failed** deployment (and only that): **Roll back** opens the plan for the version and parameters of the server's current files (the latest succeeded deployment with `uploaded = 1`), kind `redeploy` (or `upgrade` when the version differs). | redeploy.md step 7. |
| Removed endpoint | The `endpoints` step deletes endpoint rows whose key the target lacks; the plan warned. | |
| Rollout | `servers_rollouts` + items. Started from the server list (selected servers, or "all on older versions", **Upgrade to default version**): a screen lists per server the version change and changed-file count, and the servers needing new parameter values (their inputs inline; **Start rollout** is disabled until filled). Servers already at the default are skipped (`skipped`). Items ordered by server name. Start: rollout `running`, first item enqueued (`servers.deploy`, kind `upgrade`, `rollout_id`), `server.rollout_started{servers, to_version}`. | redeploy.md "rolling upgrade". |
| Rollout progress | Subscriber `servers.rollout` on `server.redeployed` and `server.redeploy_failed` with a `rollout` in the payload. It acts only when the item is still `running` with that event's job id (delivery is at least once). Success → item `done`; if the rollout is still `running`, the next item is enqueued in the same transaction; failure (a cancelled job included) → item `failed`, rollout `stopped`, the rest stay `waiting` (shown "not started"). Last item done → rollout `done`. | Event-driven: no job holds a provisioning worker while waiting. |
| Stop rollout | Strength 1. Rollout → `cancelled` at once, so no new item starts; the running item (if any) finishes on its own and the subscriber records its result. | |
| Rollout end | `server.rollout_finished{state, done, failed, not_started}` and `finished_at` are written exactly once, when the rollout is no longer `running` **and** no item is `running`: by the subscriber for `done`/`stopped` and for a `cancelled` rollout whose item just ended, or by **Stop rollout** itself when no item runs. | A stopped rollout must still report its end. |
| Rollout of a server that changed meanwhile | When its item starts, a server no longer active or already at the target is `skipped` with the reason. | |
| Restart stack | `servers.restart`: steps `restart` (`docker compose restart`), `self-check`. Deployment kind `restart` (no files). `server.redeployed{kind: restart}`. | redeploy.md table. |
| Update images | `servers.update_images`: `images-before` (`docker compose images --format json` → image IDs), `pull`, `up`, `images-after`, `self-check`, `proxy-test`. `changed_images` = services whose image ID changed. Kind `images`. | |
| Reboot | `servers.reboot`: `reboot` (`sudo -n systemctl reboot`, connection drop expected), `wait-ssh` (reconnect every 10 s, 5 min timeout), `self-check`, `proxy-test`. Kind `reboot`. The stats delta rules (1f) see the uptime drop. | |
| Container logs | `servers.container_logs`: one step, `docker compose logs --no-color --tail 200 <service>` per service into the job log. No deployment, no event. Allowed on **active and failed** servers (failed: when the stack was uploaded). The button opens the job page. | |
| Light ops failure | Their `OnFailed` records `server.redeploy_failed{kind, step, error}` like deploys. | |
| Rotation job | `servers.rotate`: steps `generate` (new values for `rotate: true` keys into `servers_generated_values.pending`, sealed; a resumed run keeps existing pending values), `upload-files` (render with pending values), `redeploy` (the version's redeploy steps), `proxy-test` (every endpoint rendered with pending values must pass), `commit` (one `Write`: `value = pending`, `pending = NULL`, `rotated_at`; endpoints re-rendered and stored; deployment `succeeded`; `server.credentials_rotated{keys}`). Deployment kind `rotate`. | rotation.md. |
| Rotation failure | A failure in `upload-files`, `redeploy` or `proxy-test` runs **restore** inside that step before returning the error: re-upload the server's current files (a deployment row of kind `restore`, `uploaded = 1`), run the redeploy steps, proxy test with the old values, clear `pending`. The same procedure is the job type `servers.restore` (steps `upload-files`, `redeploy`, `proxy-test`, `clear-pending`), used after a cancelled rotation. `OnFailed` records `server.redeploy_failed{kind: rotate, step, error, restored}` (`restored` false when the restore itself failed; the log says what is on the server). | "Old values stay in force until the new ones pass." |
| Old URIs during rotation | Ports and pages read `value`, never `pending`, so subscribers and the page serve the old URI until `commit`. | Edge case "fetch during the job". |
| Rotate dialog | Strength 2: the keys that change, "N links in M subscriptions serve this server" from `UsageReader` (Phase 1: "Subscriptions aren't built yet; no links are affected"), and rotation.md's warning text. | |
| Stack tab | The deployment holding the current files (latest succeeded with `uploaded = 1`): version, time, kind, files (tree; masked highlighted content; **Reveal** per file, admin); history table of every deployment (kind, versions, state, files changed, job link, **Diff** with the previous deployment that uploaded files, on rows that uploaded files). | ui/README. |
| Actions availability | Redeploy, Upgrade, Edit parameters, Rotate, Restart stack, Update images, Reboot: active only. Upgrade shown when another version exists ("update available" when the default is newer). Container logs: active, or failed with a deployment. All are `ui.Action`s on the server page's "more" menu and in the palette. | modules/servers.md. |

## Go signatures

```go
package deploy

type Target struct {
	Kind    string // redeploy upgrade params
	Version int
	Params  map[string]string
	Force   bool
}
type FileChange struct {
	Path, Change string // added changed removed
	ModeFrom, ModeTo fs.FileMode
	Diff        string // masked unified
}
type EndpointChange struct {
	Key, Change string // added removed changed
	URIChanged  bool
}
type Plan struct {
	ServerID               int64
	FromVersion, ToVersion int
	Files         []FileChange
	NewGenerated  []string
	Endpoints     []EndpointChange
	ParamsAdded, ParamsRemoved []string
	MissingParams []string // required, no default, not given
	Steps         []string
	Warnings      []string
	Empty         bool
	Hash          string
}
func (s *Service) Plan(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, t Target) (Plan, error)
func (s *Service) Apply(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, t Target, planHash, actor string) (jobID int64, err error)
func (s *Service) RollBack(ctx context.Context, serverID int64) (Target, error)
func (s *Service) Restart(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) (int64, error)
func (s *Service) UpdateImages(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) (int64, error)
func (s *Service) Reboot(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) (int64, error)
func (s *Service) ContainerLogs(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) (int64, error)
func (s *Service) Rotate(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, actor string) (int64, error)

type RolloutItemPlan struct {
	ServerID      int64
	Name          string
	From, To      int
	FilesChanged  int
	MissingParams []string
	Skip          string // reason, "" = will run
}
func (s *Service) PlanRollout(ctx context.Context, serverIDs []int64) ([]RolloutItemPlan, error)
func (s *Service) StartRollout(ctx context.Context, serverIDs []int64, params map[int64]map[string]string, actor string) (rolloutID int64, err error)
func (s *Service) StopRollout(ctx context.Context, id int64, actor string) error
func (s *Service) Subscriber() events.Subscriber // servers.rollout
func (s *Service) JobTypes() []jobs.Type
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /servers/:id/redeploy` | Plan for the current version |
| `GET /servers/:id/upgrade?version=N` | Version picker + parameters, then the plan |
| `GET /servers/:id/params` | Parameters form, then the plan |
| `POST /servers/:id/plan` | Plan fragment for posted target |
| `POST /servers/:id/apply` | Apply (target + plan hash) → server page |
| `GET /servers/:id/rollback` | Plan of the roll back |
| `POST /servers/:id/restart`, `/images`, `/reboot`, `/logs` | Light ops (strength 1; reboot strength 2) → job page for logs, server page otherwise |
| `GET /servers/:id/rotate`, `POST /servers/:id/rotate` | Rotate dialog / start |
| `GET /servers/:id/stack` | Stack tab |
| `GET /servers/:id/stack/files/:deployment/*path` | Revealed file (no-store) |
| `GET /servers/:id/stack/diff/:deployment` | Diff with the previous uploading deployment |
| `POST /servers/rollout/plan` | Rollout screen for selected servers |
| `POST /servers/rollout` | Start → `/servers/rollouts/:id` |
| `GET /servers/rollouts/:id` | Per-server progress table (live via htmx polling every 2 s while running) |
| `POST /servers/rollouts/:id/stop` | Stop |

## Events

Recorded: `server.redeployed`, `server.redeploy_failed`, `server.credentials_rotated`, `server.rollout_started`, `server.rollout_finished`. Notification texts per events.md (`server.redeploy_failed` and `server.credentials_rotated` notify).

## Doc changes in the same commit

- `docs/processes/servers/server-redeploy.md`: the rollout is advanced by events; **Stop rollout**; skipped servers; container logs allowed on failed servers with a stack.
- `docs/processes/servers/credential-rotation.md`: restore runs inside the failing step; the `restored` flag; cut-off waits for Phase 2.
- `docs/events.md`: `server.redeployed` payload gains `rollout` and `changed_images`; `server.redeploy_failed` gains `restored` and `cancelled` (cancelled ones don't notify); `server.rollout_finished` gains `state`.
- `docs/processes/servers/server-redeploy.md`: plans and Roll back compare with the latest deployment that uploaded files; a cancelled deploy fails its deployment; a cancelled rotation is restored by a `servers.restore` job.

## Checklist

Plans and deploys, in `deploy/` (Harness from 1d):

- [x] Redeploy with nothing changed → "Nothing to change", no job unless Force — `plan_test.go` `TestNothingToChange`
- [x] Upgrade v1 → v2 changing only `site/index.html` → plan shows one file; job uploads it and runs `compose up`; URIs unchanged — `deploy_test.go` `TestUpgradeOneFile`
- [x] v2 adds parameter `log_level` without a default → asked before the plan — `plan_test.go` `TestMissingParameterAskedFirst`
- [x] v2 adds generated value `stats_token` → created at upgrade and listed in the plan — `deploy_test.go` `TestUpgradeCreatesGeneratedValue`
- [x] v2 removes `site/extra.css` → plan lists it removed; job deletes it; `certbot/conf/` untouched — `deploy_test.go` `TestUpgradeRemovesOldFile`
- [x] v2 drops endpoint `main` → plan warning; after apply the endpoint is gone from `EndpointCatalog` — `deploy_test.go` `TestDroppedEndpointDisappears`
- [x] Server unreachable → fails at connect; server files unchanged — `deploy_test.go` `TestUnreachableFailsAtConnect`
- [x] `compose up` fails → `server.redeploy_failed`; **Roll back** offered and its plan targets the last good version — `deploy_test.go` `TestComposeFailureOffersRollBack`
- [x] A redeploy requested while another mutating job on the server runs → runs after it — `deploy_test.go` `TestDeploysAreSerializedPerServer`
- [x] The plan changed between preview and apply → the job logs the recomputation and applies the new difference — `deploy_test.go` `TestPlanIsRecomputed`
- [x] A changed host key → fails "host key changed" before uploading — `deploy_test.go` `TestHostKeyChangedStopsDeploy`
- [x] A redeploy never asks for the root password — `deploy_test.go` `TestRedeployUsesOnlyProxiersKey`
- [x] Diffs and plans never contain a generated value or secret parameter — `mask_test.go` `TestPlansAreMasked`
- [x] Edit parameters changes the stored params only on success — `deploy_test.go` `TestParamsChangeOnlyOnSuccess`
- [x] Restart stack after an upgrade, then Redeploy → "Nothing to change" (the restart deployment is not the current files); Roll back targets the upgrade's version — `plan_test.go` `TestPlanIgnoresDeploymentsWithoutFiles`
- [x] Cancel a running deploy → deployment `failed` (`cancelled`), `server.redeploy_failed{cancelled: true}`, no notification — `deploy_test.go` `TestCancelledDeployFailsDeployment`

Rollouts, in `deploy/rollout_test.go`:

- [x] Five servers, the third fails its proxy test → two done, one failed, two not started; rollout stopped; one `server.rollout_finished` — `TestRolloutStopsAtFirstFailure`
- [x] Servers run one at a time in name order — `TestRolloutRunsInNameOrder`
- [x] A server needing a parameter blocks the start until given — `TestRolloutNeedsParameters`
- [x] Stop rollout → the running item finishes, nothing new starts, then one `server.rollout_finished{state: cancelled}`; Stop with no item running finishes at once — `TestStopRollout`
- [x] The running item's job is cancelled → item `failed`, rollout `stopped`, finished — `TestCancelledItemStopsRollout`
- [x] The same `server.redeployed` delivered twice → the next item is enqueued once — `TestRolloutSubscriberIsIdempotent`
- [x] A server already at the target is skipped — `TestRolloutSkipsCurrentServers`

Light operations, in `deploy/ops_test.go`:

- [x] Restart stack restarts and self-checks; `server.redeployed{kind: restart}` — `TestRestartStack`
- [x] Update images where no image changed → succeeds with `changed_images: []` — `TestUpdateImagesNoChange`
- [x] Reboot where SSH doesn't come back within 5 min → fails — `TestRebootTimeout`
- [x] Container logs write 200 lines per service into the job log, record no event — `TestContainerLogs`

Rotation, in `deploy/rotate_test.go`:

- [x] Rotate → UUID and path change; the old URI fails the proxy test, the new one passes — `TestRotateChangesCredentials`
- [x] The catalog right after commit serves the new URI; during the job (before commit) the old — `TestRotationVisibleOnlyAfterCommit`
- [x] Upload of new files fails → old files restored, old values stay, the event names the step — `TestRotationUploadFailureRestores`
- [x] Proxy test with the new values fails → restored and redeployed; afterwards the old values pass — `TestRotationProxyFailureRestores`
- [x] Only `rotate: true` values change; `container_postfix` stays — `TestOnlyRotatableValuesChange`
- [x] Rotating a server in no subscription → allowed; the dialog says no links are affected — `pages/deploy_test.go` `TestRotateDialogWithoutSubscriptions`
- [x] Rotation requested while a redeploy runs → waits, then runs — `TestRotationWaitsForRedeploy`
- [x] A restart during `proxy-test` resumes with the same pending values — `TestRotationResumesWithSamePending`
- [x] Cancel a rotation after `upload-files` → `servers.restore` queued; it re-uploads the old files, the old values pass, `pending` is cleared — `TestCancelledRotationIsRestored`

- [x] Plan screen shows files, new values, endpoint changes, warnings; Apply goes to the server page — `TestPlanScreen`

## As built

Done 2026-10-08. Every checklist line has its test, in the file the line names. `make test`, `make lint` (0 issues), `go vet` and gofmt are green; `docker build .` and `make check` results are in the commit's report. Deviations and notes for 1f and later:

- **Packages.** `servers/deploy` (`service.go` the service, seams and the job types; `plan.go`; `deploy.go` the `servers.deploy` steps; `ops.go`; `rotate.go` with the restore; `rollout.go`; `mask.go`), pages `deploy.go`, `rollout.go`, `stack.go` and `server_{plan,rollout,stack,rotate}.templ`. `Module.Deploy` is built in `Init`; its **seams are provisioning's** (`ProxyTest`, `ProxyOptions`, `RemoteEnv`, `SmokeAttempts`, `SmokeGap`, read at use), so a test replaces them once. `module.SubscriberDeclarer` is implemented for the first time (`servers.rollout`). `deploy` joined `XRAY_TESTS` (the rotation test pushes real XHTTP traffic); the other deploy tests use `serverstest.StubProxy()`.
- **Signatures that changed.**
  - `Plan` gained `Kind`, `Force`, `UploadCount`, `ParamsChanged`, `Problems` (the parameter values the version refuses, by field); `Warnings` is `[]Msg` (i18n key + arguments), not `[]string`; `Steps` are job step names; `FileChange` gained `SecretOnly` (only a secret differs, so the masked diff is empty), `OldSize`, `NewSize`. `FieldErrors` and `Msg` are aliases of provisioning's, so the pages translate both the same way.
  - **`RollBack` returns a *forced* target** (the version and parameters of the current files, `Force: true`). The stored current files are the last *succeeded* deployment's, so a roll back that was not forced would compare equal to them and say "Nothing to change", although the failed deployment had put other files on the server. `CanRollBack` is the page's question.
  - `RolloutItemPlan` gained `Problem` (the version does not render for the server; **Start** refuses while one has it); `PlanRolloutWith` takes the values typed on the screen. `StartRollout` answers `FieldErrors` named `server.<id>.param.<key>`. A rollout takes the servers of **one template** (`ErrMixedTemplates`): `servers_rollouts` has one template and one target version.
  - Also exported: `RotatableKeys`, `StoredSecrets`, `DiffMaskers`, `Masker` / `Secrets` / `NewMasker` / `Mask`, `ErrNotActive`, `ErrNothingToChange`, `ErrNoRollBack`, `ErrNothingToRotate`, `ErrNotAllowed`, `RenderError`.
- **Masking.** `Secrets` holds several values per key, because an old deployment's files were rendered with values a rotation replaced. A secret that differs between the two sides of a diff is `•••key (old)•••` / `•••key (new)•••`; one that does not is `•••key•••`. **The deployment's sealed blob (`deployment:<id>:params`) now also holds the generated values its files were rendered with** (`sealed.DeploymentSecrets{Params, Gen}`, format `{"v":2,…}`; the first format, a flat map, still opens as `Params`). Without it the Stack tab could not mask a pre-rotation deployment: the old UUID is gone from `servers_generated_values`. Provisioning writes it too. The plan hash is over the *masked* new contents, so it is stable although new generated values are made afresh by every plan.
- **Plan details.** A secret parameter left blank in a form keeps its stored value. A plan whose only difference is a changed parameter (nothing in any file) is not empty. Removals are computed against the current deployment's files only: a file a *failed* deployment added and the current set lacks stays on the server until a Force redeploy or a restore (a restore does remove it). `Upload` carries only added and changed files unless forced; `previous` for `remote.UploadFiles` is the removal list, so an unchanged file is never deleted.
- **Jobs.**
  - `servers.deploy`'s `plan` step logs "The plan was recomputed: …" when its hash differs from the shown one, and sets `noop` when nothing is left to change (the other steps then do nothing and no event is recorded). Each step recomputes the target from the stored state (steps are idempotent; a resumed job finds its running deployment by kind).
  - Light operations have a final `record` step (the contract's step lists had none); the deployment and its event are written there, so a failure in between leaves a `failed` deployment. **Every change's self-check is tried up to four times (`CheckGap`, 5 s; a reboot 12 times)** because containers that were just recreated need a moment; provisioning's is unchanged. Reboot reads `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` before and after (`remote.CmdBootID`), so a reconnect to a machine that has not gone down yet is not taken for the reboot. `RebootPoll` / `RebootTimeout` are fields (10 s / 5 min).
  - Rotation: `generate` **always starts from new values** (it clears `pending` first; a resumed job does not run it again because the step succeeded), instead of "a resumed run keeps existing pending values". The restore after a failed `upload-files`, `redeploy` or `proxy-test` runs inside that step (`restoreOnError`) unless the admin cancelled or the process is stopping, saves `restored` in the payload, and **always drops the pending values**, even when the restore failed (the log then says the server may hold new files; Redeploy fixes it). `restoreOnError` is skipped on cancel/shutdown because those paths restore on their own (`servers.restore` queued in `OnCancelled`; a resumed job runs the step again). `jobs.System.LogLine(ctx, tx, jobID, level, text)` lets `OnCancelled` write "restore queued as job #N" into a job that already ended.
  - `server.redeployed{kind: restore}` is recorded by the `servers.restore` job only; the in-step restore records nothing of its own (`server.redeploy_failed{restored}` is its report).
  - The rollout event subject is `rollout:<id>` (not `server`), so `Module.SubjectTypes` and `NameSubjects` know `rollout` and `/servers/rollouts/:id` is its link. `server.rollout_finished` also carries `skipped`. `Stop rollout` of a rollout whose item is running leaves `finished_at` empty until the subscriber sees the item end.
- **Pages.**
  - Plan screens are **whole pages**, not fragments: `POST /servers/:id/plan` answers the same page as `GET …/upgrade`, `…/params`, `…/redeploy`, `…/rollback`. It works without JavaScript; the plan's hash and the typed values travel as hidden fields of the Apply form (the page is `no-store`). The form for an upgrade or a parameter edit sits above the plan; when parameters are missing only the form shows.
  - The server page has an **Actions area** (not a "more" menu): Roll back (when offered), Upgrade (when another version exists; "update available"), Edit parameters, Rotate credentials, Restart stack, Update images, Reboot, Container logs; **Redeploy…** is the primary button of the header. Restart, Update images and Reboot confirm in the usual dialog (Reboot strength 2); Upgrade, Edit parameters and Rotate open their own pages. A change in progress (or `?job=<id>`, where Apply and the operations redirect to) shows its steps and live log on the page like provisioning does. A latest failed deployment that uploaded files shows a band with **Roll back…**. The identity area says "v3 is available" next to the version.
  - **Rotate is a page** (`GET /servers/:id/rotate`: keys, links from `UsageReader`, the warning, **Rotate**), not a dialog; the page is the confirmation. Without `UsageReader` it says "Subscriptions aren't built yet; no links are affected."
  - **Rollouts start from the template page** ("Servers on older versions", **Upgrade all to vN…**, which posts the active older servers to `POST /servers/rollout/plan`). The server list gets its bulk action with the selection in 1g; `POST /servers/rollout/plan` accepts any `server` ids. **Start rollout** is a disabled button while a server still needs a value, next to **Check the values** (a second plan request with what was typed), so it works without JavaScript. The progress table polls itself every two seconds (`hx-select`) until the rollout has ended.
  - Stack tab: the file tree (directories as rows), highlighted masked content, **Reveal** swaps the code block for the real file (`no-store`), the history table with **Job**, **Diff** (the previous succeeded deployment that uploaded files) and **Roll back…**. The diff page masks both sides with `DiffMaskers`.
- **Platform / test seams.** `jobs.System.LogLine`; `sshx.SSH.Dial` (a test replaces the TCP dial; nothing in production sets it) so the harness's `AddServer(ip)` can have many servers on one fake VPS (`VPS.Unharden` gives root's password back for the next provisioning); `VPS.Fail(op, msg, times)`, `NewImage`, `Reboots`, `RebootNeverReturns`, `RebootDowntime`, boot ids, `AnyFileContains`; `Harness.ProxyAccepts` / `FollowVPS` (which endpoints the stub or real proxy test accepts), `StopDispatcher`, `LastJob`. **The harness now runs the event dispatcher** (rollouts move on events). `app.css` gained the plan, rollout and Stack rules.
- **Docs changed:** `server-redeploy.md`, `credential-rotation.md`, `events.md`, `modules/servers.md`, `data-model.md` (as the contract's Doc changes list says, plus the pending value, the deployment's secrets and rollouts).
- **Not done / for the user.**
  - **No command added here has run on a real server**: `docker compose restart`, `images --format json`, `logs --no-color --tail 200 <service>`, `systemctl reboot`, `cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, and the whole redeploy and rotation flow, are only parsed and answered by `serverstest.VPS`. In particular `docker compose images --format json` prints an array on some Compose versions and one object per line on others (both are read), but its field names (`ContainerName`, `Repository`, `Tag`, `ID`) are from the documentation.
  - **No page was opened in a real browser**: the plan screen and its Apply/Force dialogs, the Actions area, the Stack tab's Reveal swap, the rollout page's polling and the new CSS are only tested server side.
  - The Rotate-then-restore path and a reboot were tested with a fake that cannot tell what a real nginx or xray would do with half-uploaded files.
- **Notes for 1f.** Deploy jobs hold `server:<id>` as the README says; `jobs.System.Busy` is still 1f's to add. The self-check inside a change goes through `deploy.Service.selfCheck` (with retries) and writes no `servers_check_results` row: 1f's health may record one from these jobs if it wants a fresh result right after a change. `server.redeployed` is the event to re-evaluate health on (`kind`, `rollout`), and `server.credentials_rotated`'s `keys` for subscriptions. A deployment's `kind` list is complete (`provision redeploy upgrade params rotate restore restart images reboot`); the stats delta rules see the reboot as an uptime drop.
